branchModel.main: our version of the latest upstream release pin: the pin plus our adapted patches. Dev builds come from here continuously.
branchModel.release: a release is a semver tag on main, unique to Nucleo and never upstream's version. Nothing publishes without a green gate on that commit.
branchModel.pinBump: bumping the pin is a minor-or-major version event: the pin change and the patch adaptation land together.

versioning: 0.0.0 is the starting dev line, not a release. The first release is v0.0.1. A release bumps the version and tags it on main; main itself always carries the next unreleased version.
gatesNote: Each name is a pnpm script in the pinned repo, except 'tests', which runs distro/scripts/patch-tests.mjs: every carried patch's own tests, from its upstream PR. Upstream's full suite is not re-run here, because upstream already runs it before every release; we test what our patches change. 'typecheck' does not exist upstream (ERR_PNPM_NO_SCRIPT made a false red), so the aggregate check is 'check'.
_pathsNote: This committed manifest is the only copy. Host values (checkout, logs, alert script) live in nucleo.local.json beside it, which is gitignored; these values are shape, not any host paths.
devBuildNumber: one more than the highest v<version>-dev.<n> tag on the fork, and a commit that already carries a dev tag keeps its number; scripts/build-number.mjs owns the rule, and CI computes it once per run and passes it on as NUCLEO_BUILD_NUMBER
lintScopeNeutralPathsNote: Paths a carried patch edits without changing any lint rule or cap. perf/oxlint-extension-chunk-size only sizes lint chunks for the host; naming its file keeps upstream's changed-file lint scoping on, so line caps that upstream treats as advisory for files we never touched stay advisory here.
cachesNote: Bounds for what a host running the gate or build keeps between runs. cache-bound.mjs trims the Node compile cache and the Vitest module cache least recently used first before a run, and the image build trims the docker build cache to dockerBuildMaxGb after it, so a repeat run stays warm and the disk stays bounded.
